title: SARS-CoV-2 proteome microarray for COVID-19 patient sera profiling
protocol: Express recombinant proteins in E. coli BL21 by growing cells in 200 mL LB medium to an A600 of 0.6 at 37°C.
Add 0.2 mM IPTG and incubate cells for 16 h at 16°C.
Re-suspend cell pellets in lysis buffer and lyse using a high-pressure cell cracker.
Centrifuge the cell lysates at 12,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Affinity purify supernatants with Ni2+ Sepharose beads.
Wash Ni2+ Sepharose beads with lysis buffer and elute proteins using a buffer containing 10% glycerol, 50 mM Tris-HCl pH8.0, 500 mM NaCl, and 300 mM imidazole.
Verify purified proteins by SDS-PAGE followed by western blotting using an anti-His antibody.
Stain the gel with Coomassie brilliant blue to visualize the purified proteins.
Reconstitute recombinant SARS-CoV-2 protein from commercial sources.
Transfer proteins and controls to a 384-well plate.
Dilute the proteins and controls with printing buffer to a final concentration of 0.3 mg/mL.
Add diluted proteins into predetermined wells in the 384-well plate.
Centrifuge the 384-well plate at 800 × g for 1 minute at 4°C.
Store the protein-containing plate at -80°C for long-term storage if not immediately used.
Use the printer to print proteins onto PATH substrate slides according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Incubate the microarrays at 4°C with humidity less than 50% overnight (over 12 hours) for complete immobilization of proteins on the microarray.
Put the slides into the dedicated slide box, placing either one or five slides per box.
Seal the box with Parafilm and store the box at −80°C.
Create an Excel file to mark the position of samples on a 380-well plate.
Take out the microarrays from −80°C and leave them at 4°C for 30 minutes, then transfer them to room temperature for 15 minutes to allow temperature equilibrium.
Prepare the blocking buffer (1× PBS with 3% BSA), adding 30 mL of buffer to a container and keeping it at 25°C.
Face down the microarray and immerse the barcode side into the blocking buffer, leaving the other side out.
Slowly lay down the microarray until it is completely immersed in the buffer.
Gently shake the microarray to ensure that all bubbles on its surface are removed.
Turn over the microarray and immerse it into the buffer.
Shake the microarrays at 20–30 rpm/min on a shaker for 3 hours at 25°C.
Wash and dry the microarrays.
Discard the blocking buffer.
Add 20–30 mL of 1× PBS into the container, keep shaking (20–30 rpm) for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Discard the PBS buffer.
Add 20–30 mL of 0.2× PBS into the container, keep shaking (20–30 rpm) for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Discard the PBS buffer.
Add 20–30 mL of ddH₂O into the container, keep shaking (20–30 rpm) for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Centrifuge the microarrays at 500 × g for 1–2 minutes to dry them.
Store dried microarrays at 4°C in a sealed box.
Prepare incubation buffer by diluting Anti-His antibody at 1:5000 in PBST buffer (0.1% Tween 20 in 1× PBS buffer).
Add 3 mL of incubation buffer into the microarray slide container.
Shake the container at 4°C and 20–30 rpm for 12 hours.
Discard the incubation buffer.
Add 5 mL PBST buffer, shake at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Repeat the previous step three times.
Prepare secondary antibody by diluting Cy5 labeled Anti-Rabbit secondary antibody at a ratio of 1:1000 in PBST buffer.
Add the secondary antibody into the microarray slide container, shake at 25°C for 1 hour.
Discard the incubation buffer.
Add 5 mL PBST buffer and shake at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Repeat this step three times.
Dry the microarrays by centrifugation with SlideWashTM 8.
Centrifuge the microarrays at 500 × g for 1–2 minutes.
Turn on the microarray scanner Genepix 4200A and warm up for 15 minutes.
Scan the microarray at both 532 nm (IgG) and 635 nm (IgM) channel.
Save the two images as a single TIF file.
Centrifuge the tube with sera at 12,000 × g at 4°C for 20 minutes.
Dilute the sera in incubation buffer which contains 1% BSA and 0.1% Tween 20 in 1× PBS (1:200).
Install a 16-well chamber on the microarray to physically separate the subarrays.
Dilute the sera sample and the positive control at a ratio of 1:200 with incubation buffer (1× PBS with 0.1% tween-20 and 1% BSA).
Add 200 μL of diluted serum sample to each subarray.
Incubate the last two subarrays with incubation buffer and positive sera as blank control and positive control, respectively.
Incubate the microarrays at room temperature (25°C) for 2 h.
Remove the sera from each subarray using a multichannel pipette.
Add 200 μL of wash buffer to each subarray and pipette up and down ten times.
Repeat the washing step twice more.
Uninstall the 16-well chamber, place microarrays in a container with approximately 30 mL of wash buffer.
Shake the container at room temperature (25°C) for 10 min using a shaker set to 90–100 rpm.
Repeat this washing step twice more.
Do not allow the surface of the slides to dry during handling.
Dilute Cy3 labeled anti-Human IgG and Alexa Fluor 647 (635 nm excitation) labeled anti-Human IgM secondary antibodies at a ratio of 1:1000 with incubation buffer.
Discard wash buffer from the container, add 15 mL of diluted secondary antibodies.
Shake the container on a shaker set to 20–30 rpm for 1 h at room temperature (25°C).
Keep microarrays shielded from light during secondary antibody incubation.
Remove the solution from the container and add 30 mL Wash buffer.
Shake the container for 90–100 rpm on a shaker for 10 min at room temperature (25°C).
Repeat the wash step three times with 30 mL Wash buffer.
Wash the slide with ddH2O for 10 min.
Rinse the slide with ddH2O for 10 s.
Dry the slide by centrifugation.
Turn on the microarray scanner Genepix 4200A and warm up for 15 min.
Scan the microarray at 532 nm (IgG) and 635 nm (IgM) channel.
Save the result as one single TIF file.
Extract microarray data using Genepix 6.0 software.
Align the features of the microarray image using the GAL file.
Double-check and adjust incorrectly aligned features.
Click the “analysis” button to extract all feature data.
Generate a GPR file for each microarray.
Calculate signal intensity by subtracting Background Median from Foreground Median.
Calculate IgG (532 nm channel) signal intensity separately.
Calculate IgM (635 nm channel) signal intensity separately.
Calculate the average of triplicates of each protein in the same subarray.
Use data from block #14 to calculate normalization factor for each microarray.
Exclude features with low signal intensity (< 300).
Calculate the overall average signal intensity for each protein from block #14 microarrays (excluding controls).
Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between the reference data set and each block #14 data set.
Exclude spots where the coefficient is less than 0.98.
Use Excel's LINEST function to calculate Factor N: LINEST(Y, X i, FALSE), with Y as the reference data set and X i as the data from slide i.
Normalize all signal intensities for each slide by multiplying them with the corresponding Factor N.
